newsitem.title: RUSSIA: OLYMPICS-ST PETERSBURG PRESSES BID TO HOST 2004 GAMES.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-ST PETERSBURG PRESSES BID TO HOST 2004 GAMES.

text.p: International Olympic Committee (IOC) president Juan Antonio Samaranch arrived in Moscow on Friday as Russian officials pressed their bid to have St. Petersburg chosen as host for the 2004 Olympics.

Russia's second city of five million is one of 11 candidates vying for the 2004 Games. The others are Rome, Cape Town, Stockholm, Rio de Janeiro, San Juan, Buenos Aires, Athens, Lille, Seville and Istanbul. The IOC will decide on a short list in March and the winner in September.
"For me, as the president of the IOC, there is no leading candidate," Samaranch said when asked about St. Petersburg's prospects. "All the candidates have an equal chance."
Samaranch was met at the airport by Vice-Premier Viktor Ilyushin, the president of the Russian Olympic Committee and the Mayor of St. Petersburg, Itar-Tass reported.
He then attended a New Year's party in the Kremlin for Russia's Olympic athletes and their trainers.
On Saturday he is expected to meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
